rows.criterion: Two public learner/advisor pairs were completed
rows.reason: An early stop or missing reply remains incomplete, rather than being padded with a transcript.

rows.criterion: Both replies are valid public answers
rows.reason: Checks empty/error/pseudo-tool output independently of transport success.

rows.criterion: Original identity and revision are preserved
rows.reason: Saved provenance does not establish population coverage.

rows.criterion: The follow-up asks about game design
rows.reason: The actual UserSim follow-up must exercise the intended distinction.

rows.criterion: The frozen catalogue has no board-game playing class
rows.reason: This is a dated catalogue result, not a claim about every provider.

rows.criterion: The first reply acknowledges a catalogue limit
rows.reason: A narrow phrase check; review the linked reply for nuance.

rows.criterion: Any cited course IDs exist in the snapshot
rows.reason: Does not certify unsupported claims without a course identifier.

rows.criterion: Playing and designing games are distinguished
rows.reason: Checks selected explicit distinction phrases, including a non-negated separate skill set in the same sentence as board-game play and game design; not complete semantic or pedagogical quality.

rows.criterion: Any cited course IDs exist in the snapshot
rows.reason: Does not certify unsupported claims without a course identifier.

rows.criterion: Both replies use the same persistent native thread
rows.reason: Same-thread identity plus the follow-up checks persistence; it is not proof of cross-session memory.

rows.criterion: A completed native catalogue search is attributable
rows.reason: Application intent logs cannot replace native tool execution.

coverage: Two public pairs, explicit no-match/design distinction, valid answers, known IDs, same native thread and actual tool evidence. Semantic recommendation quality still requires review.
